comments.author: ghoward
comments.story_title: What’s the end goal for you programmers?
comments.why_zh: 关于软件专业性和服务用户的演讲
comments.text_zh: 我并不在工业界工作；我是个特别独行的程序员，在工业界里很挣扎。但因为我妻子喜欢她的工作，我有空间去写我想写的软件。我的第一个目标是让那个软件足够好、足够有用，从而创建一家像 Hwaci 那样只做工程的公司，Hwaci 就是做 SQLite 和 Fossil 的公司。如果我成功了，我会看看能不能赚到足够的钱提前退休，并通过我的教会做慈善工作。但我在工业界期间还有另一个目标。我想改变我们这个行业，让它成为一个有职业道德准则的专业行业，让我们创造出服务用户、而不是服务雇主或政府的软件。这意味着要反对收集用户数据、投放广告，以及其他让软件违背用户意愿、服从其创造者的做法。我甚至创建了一个 Twitter 账号来展示其中一些东西。[1] 是的，这意味着要跟几乎所有 Big Tech 打一场硬仗，我并不指望能赢。但如果我能让人们思考这件事，我就会把这当作胜利。但无论如何，我对此感受强烈，因为用户依赖我们做出服务他们的软件。如果我们不做，就没有人会做。Uncle Bob Martin 谈过这个。[2]（那个链接从一个不错的点开始，但整个演讲都值得一看。）所以这就是我的目标：做出好软件，并让行业变得更好。是很崇高，没错，但只要能完成其中一个目标，我就会满意。[1]: [LINK] [2]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: I am not working in industry; I'm such a loner programmer that I struggle in industry. But since my wife likes her work, I have space to write the software I want to write. My first goal is to make that software good enough and useful enough to create an engineering-only company like Hwaci, the company that does SQLite and Fossil. If I succeed at that, I'll see about trying to pull in enough money to retire early and do charity work through my church. But I have another goal for while I'm still in industry. I want to change our industry such that it is a professional industry, with a code of ethics, to where we create software that serves users , not our employers or government. This means fighting against slurping up user data, serving ads, and other ways that software disobeys users in favor of obeying its creators. I even created a Twitter account to show some of those things. [1] Yes, that means an uphill battle against basically all of Big Tech, and I don't expect to win. But if I make people think about it, I'll take that as a win. But regardless, I feel strongly about it because users depend on us to make software that will serve them. If we don't, no one will. Uncle Bob Martin talked about this. [2] (That link starts at a good point, but the whole talk is worth watching.) So that's my goal: make good software and change the industry for the better. Lofty, yes, but I'll be satisfied by completing one of those goals. [1]: [LINK] [2]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: EdSharkey
comments.story_title: My Response to “Are we overcomplicating software development?”
comments.why_zh: 关于专业标准和监管的思考
comments.quote_zh: Uncle Bob 最近在这方面分享了一些很好的思考。
comments.text_zh: 对我来说，真正的问题在于管理者们把敏捷抓在了手里。我确信，大多数管理者想要的只是瀑布式，我怀疑关于敏捷的那么多困惑正源于此。我们开发者在制定、推广和规范化我们的标准与实践中做得糟透了。因为团队、行业、人员和项目各不相同，所以敏捷的东西需要保持宽松，这是一回事。但我们甚至没有尝试为测试驱动开发、大型可视化图表或冲刺这类通用话题建立明确的定义。坦率地说，我们需要行业领导力，以及为开发者工艺设立有公信力的认证。Uncle Bob 最近在这方面分享了一些很好的思考。他不仅建议了我们专业开发者需要前进的方向，还推测了如果我们不这样做会发生什么（失去自由）。[VIDEO]
comments.text: To me, the real issue is that the managers got ahold of agile. Most managers just want waterfall, I'm convinced, which I suspect is where so much of the head scratching about Agile comes from. We developers have done an abysmal job developing, socializing, and formalizing our standards and practices. Needing to keep agile things loose because teams and industries and people and projects differ is one thing. But, we don't even try to establish unambiguous definitions for general topics like test-driven development, big visible charts, or sprints. Frankly, we need industry leadership and earned certifications for developer craftsmanship. Uncle Bob recently has shared some good food for thought in this area. Not only does he recommend the direction we professional devs need to head, but he also speculates as to what will happen if we don't (loss of freedom.) [VIDEO]

comments.author: jodrellblank
comments.story_title: What does the 'rc' in `.bashrc`, etc. mean?
comments.text_zh:
> 当你花 30 秒在 Reddit 上发个帖，只为省下 3 秒的谷歌搜索时间，你到底在成就什么？

一方面，你可能看到有人说"欢迎学习西班牙语，有问题尽管问！"，然后就单纯信了，而没想到那其实是个怪胎窝，人们正等着因为你问的问题不够高明而扑上来咬你。/r/learnspanish 的侧边栏甚至写着"如果你有任何与西班牙语相关的问题，尽管问，我们会尽力帮忙！"。另一方面，学新东西的时候，你正处在自己能力的边缘——你想要的是针对这个卡点的直接答案，而不是一个"每个初学者都必须知道的 5000 个单词！"的视频，或者一页"二十个假同源词"（答案也许在里面），或者一页"西班牙语入门"（那其实是某个国家一个培训课程的广告，而且那课程根本没开课），还指望你把自己本来就紧绷的注意力挪去从一堆不相关的东西里刨出答案；就你需要的那一点提一个狭窄、聚焦的问题，可能已经是你能做到的极限了。而且就像你说的，你会去问老师，会去问朋友，会去问 IRC/Discord 之类的聊天室，那你为什么会觉得自己不能直接问 Reddit 呢？我明白，/r/powershell 里全是"我怎么把输出里的 {Name=bob} 去掉"这种问题，因为他们不理解对象管道，而我只回答我想回答的，不想回答的就忽略。
comments.text: > when you spend 30 seconds making a Reddit submission to save you 3 seconds of googling, what exactly are you accomplishing? You might have seen someone say "welcome to learning Spanish, if you have any questions just ask!" and simply believed them instead of thinking it was a sperglord den where people were waiting to jump on you for not asking superior enough questions, for one thing. The sidebar of /r/learnspanish even says " If you have a question about anything Spanish-language related, ask and we'll help the best we can! ". For another, when learning something new you're pushing the edge of what you're capable of - what you want is a direct answer to just this sticking point, not a video of "5000 words every beginner MUST know!" or a page of "Twenty False cognates" which might have the answer, or a page of "Introductory Spanish" which is an advert for a training course in another country which isn't even running and hoping you can divert your already-strained attention to digging an answer out of a lot of unrelated stuff; asking a narrow, focused question on just the thing you need might be as much as you can manage. And as you say, you would ask a teacher, you would ask a friend, you would ask an IRC/Discord/etc chat, why would you assume you can't just ask Reddit? I get it, /r/powershell is full of "how do I get rid of {Name=bob} in my output" because they don't understand the object pipeline, and I answer the ones I want to answer and ignore the ones I don't want to
